messages:
ana: quick idea: 'reserve-on-spill' for continuous batcher — don't materialize tenant soft reserves at admission. only create a reservation when an enqueue would push the merge window past the spill threshold. goal: reduce idle headroom for fleets with lots of tiny requests. want safety checks + metrics.

ty: short sketch: admission still grants optimistic credit. on enqueue if batch.size + req.tokens > spill_threshold, do ledger.CASCreateIfAbsent(batch_window, tenant, tokens) which returns reservation_id or fail. mark soft-protect TTL. promote to hard on runtime commit.

raj: pros: better packing, lower steady-state reserved tokens. cons: late reservation => cold KV/kernels => first-token tail latency. Also races: concurrent create attempts must be idempotent to avoid double-counting.

ellie: agree. invariants: 1) createIfAbsent is atomic and returns stable id on success. 2) failed create must not leak credits. 3) promotion must be observable and idempotent.

ty: ops/backstops: soft-first with short TTL (25-75ms), promotion window configurable. per-tenant create rate limit and exponential backoff on repeated evictions. circuit-breaker: if reserve_promotion_fail_rate > threshold, route tenant to eager reserves or dedicated lane.

ana: metrics to capture during canary: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_per_request, reserve_create_rate, reserve_promotion_latency, promotion_fail_rate, eviction_count, headroom_utilization.

raj: API change: admission becomes optimistic — callers must handle ErrReserveCreationFailed or ErrPreemptedByEviction. doc client retry/backoff patterns.

ellie: config sketch for experiment: 
  spill_threshold_tokens: 1600
  reserve.soft_ttl_ms: 40
  reserve.promote_after_ms: 20
  reserve.promotion_backoff_ms: 150
  reserve.max_create_per_minute: 20
  reserve.per_tenant_budget_tokens: 20000

lab-bot: scheduled experiment: pool=reserve-spill-canary start=1771240100 duration=45m.

ty: safety testing: 1) microbench with Poisson arrivals and tiny requests; 2) canary split by tenant class (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive); 3) chaos: kill host with active soft protections to verify ledger reaper cleans leaked protections.

ana: one more edge: long-running queued batches — ensure promotion doesn't starve new small tenants. add fairness check to prefer older reservations when headroom tight.

raj: i'll draft a short RFC with invariants, CAS ledger sketch, metrics, and backstop rules. will tag for review. thanks.
